response.message:
your saves are heaviest on tokyo, which is great, there's a lot to work through there. [kyoto](kebi://area/jp/kyoto) is where i'll fill the gaps, and [mount fuji](kebi://venue/67543868-5745-45bd-a5e9-4ab948480e30) sits right on the osaka-to-tokyo leg, which is the one to plan the whole route around. stop by stop:

---

kyoto

nothing saved here yet, so this one's on me. four places worth your time:

[Fushimi Inari Taisha](kebi://venue/798aea34-b234-4a06-b628-8d791d2396bf) is the one, thousands of torii gates winding up a mountain, exactly as striking in person as it looks on every video you've seen of japan. go before 8am, the crowds are brutal by mid-morning.

[Kiyomizu-dera](kebi://venue/f8d8b1da-95bf-49fc-ade3-8433f3424185) is the other must. a wooden temple platform jutting out over a hillside with views over the city. the walk up through the old higashiyama lanes is half the experience.

[Nishiki Market](kebi://venue/4137a972-fe01-4266-bbaf-3fb145d70659) is a narrow covered arcade packed with local food stalls, pickles, skewers, fresh tofu, grilled things on sticks. good for a lunch wander.

and for a matcha stop, [Gion Tsujiri](kebi://venue/eb7ecfb8-40fa-4586-9f4e-beaaf3aa5d88) is the one people go out of their way for, high-quality green tea desserts, very kyoto, very worth it.

---

osaka

you saved [Universal Studios Japan](kebi://venue/e68f1787-c5f6-4ed6-81b1-e0296a02ecf9), which is right there in osaka. full-day commitment, so give it its own day, Nintendo World is the draw right now.

beyond that, [Dotonbori](kebi://venue/1b247b82-0663-4f4f-be22-875f5ccc0a9f) is the neon canal strip, best in the evening when everything lights up. [Kuromon Market](kebi://venue/e35b0bea-bc55-4afb-adb5-a9cb8391e1b1) is your daytime food stop, more raw seafood and fresh produce than nishiki. [Osaka Castle](kebi://venue/15a9d47a-0fb6-44ec-89ac-e7fb01492588) is good for a half-morning, more for the park and the views than the museum inside.

---

on the way to tokyo, mount fuji

you saved Mount Fuji, and it sits right on this leg, which makes it the one to plan the whole route around. climbing season runs roughly july to early september so you're in the window. if you want to hike, you need a dedicated extra day, most people do the overnight climb to catch sunrise at the summit. if you just want to see it, the Kawaguchiko area gives you the classic lake reflection shot and works as a comfortable stop between osaka and tokyo.

---

tokyo

your saves here are stacked, so let me make the calls for you.

[Meiji Jingu](kebi://venue/d4104468-7ac7-4674-8b91-a9b1b559fcfb) first, calm, forested shrine in the middle of harajuku, good for an early morning before the city wakes up.

[Shinjuku Gyoen](kebi://venue/1cf8682b-9ba4-4cc1-8a07-651c8b8b7b37) for green space and quiet mid-city, you saved this one, and afternoon works perfectly. pair it with the meiji morning if you want a calm first day in tokyo.

[Shibuya Sky](kebi://venue/1bd47f5c-8855-4ba9-98e6-d4c6ccf6427f) is the rooftop observation deck above shibuya crossing, you saved this one, and sunset is the slot to book. reserve it online ahead of time, it sells out fast.

now for the teamLab question: you saved both [teamLab Planets](kebi://venue/3546d397-b212-4cb4-866a-3a87cd06c485) and [teamLab Borderless](kebi://venue/ce8d6832-b63e-4b15-8d39-50133dabbe62). they're genuinely different experiences, Planets is more intimate and physical, you walk through the installations. Borderless is larger, more overwhelming, more of an all-day wander. if you only have time for one, i'd go Planets, it's the tighter experience and easier to fit into a day. but if you have a spare afternoon, Borderless is worth it on top.

you also saved [The Making of Harry Potter](kebi://venue/3d3d35f0-b134-4c2b-9dc0-e34ecef0576e), that one is actually out in toshimaen, a bit of a trek from central tokyo. worth it if you're a fan, but it needs its own half-day. if your tokyo time is tight, it's the one i'd move to a dedicated day or cut if something has to give.

---

the whole shape of this trip comes down to how many nights you have at each stop, that decides whether kyoto gets two full days or a quick pass-through, and whether fuji is a hike or a view. how many nights are you working with, and want me to map out the days once you know?
